extracted.intended_audience: general readers and aspiring writers interested in simple living, authenticity, and craft
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive and rhetorical principles embedded in Thoreau's Walden about how to live and how to express oneself: guidance on simplicity, originality, craft, truthfulness, observation, and the value of wildness and inward exploration for writers and reflective practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need the tonic of wildness
rubrics_metrics.description: Our village life would stagnate if it were not for the unexplored forests and meadows which surround it. We need the tonic of wildness,—to wade sometimes in marshes ... We can never have enough of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exposure to wild, inexhaustible features (sea-coast with wrecks, wilderness, thunder cloud, long rain producing freshets) to refresh perspective and avoid stagnation. Examples/anti-patterns: valuing only tame, domesticated experience leads to spiritual and creative stagnation; seek scenes and experiences that reveal limits transgressed and life 'pasturing freely where we never wander.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance confidently in the direction of your dreams
rubrics_metrics.description: If one advances confidently in the direction of his dreams, and endeavors to live the life which he has imagined, he will meet with a success unexpected in common hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical effect: put some things behind, pass invisible boundaries; new, more liberal laws will establish themselves around and within you. Related advice: 'If you have built castles in the air, your work need not be lost; that is where they should be. Now put the foundations under them.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify life to clarify truth and law
rubrics_metrics.description: In proportion as he simplifies his life, the laws of the universe will appear less complex, and solitude will not be solitude, nor poverty poverty, nor weakness weakness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplification reveals universality and reduces perceived complexity. Anti-patterns: cluttered living and thought hides essential truths; practical corollary: 'Sell your clothes and keep your thoughts.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak for truth, not for facile understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a ridiculous demand which England and America make, that you shall speak so that they can understand you... I fear chiefly lest my expression may not be extra-vagant enough, may not wander far enough beyond the narrow limits of my daily experience, so as to be adequate to the truth of which I have been convinced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not level language downward to the dullest perception; allow expression to be broad, 'extra-vagant', and to betray the inadequacy of any literal statement. Anti-pattern: over-simplifying language to chase immediate comprehension at the expense of depth and fidelity to experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Say what you have to say, not what you ought
rubrics_metrics.description: Say what you have to say, not what you ought. Any truth is better than make-believe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize honesty and factuality in expression over performative or expected statements. Example/anecdote: Tom Hyde the tinker on the gallows favors plain truth rather than formulaic final words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer truth and sincerity over love, money, or fame
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than love, than money, than fame, give me truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value authenticity and sincerity in persons and works above surface elegance or social status. Example: lavish hospitality without sincerity is 'cold as the ices'—style and entertainments cannot substitute for truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drive each nail home—craft solid, finish well
rubrics_metrics.description: Drive a nail home and clinch it so faithfully that you can wake up in the night and think of your work with satisfaction,—a work at which you would not be ashamed to invoke the Muse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should be solid, well-founded, and finished with pride. Anti-patterns: superficial, half-hearted work ('foolishly drive a nail into mere lath and plastering'). Craftsmanship matters more than appearance or speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate voluntary poverty to focus on essentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate poverty like a garden herb, like sage. Do not trouble yourself much to get new things, whether clothes or friends. Turn the old; return to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poverty narrows experience to the most significant material and compels engagement with 'life near the bone.' It defends against being a trifler; superfluous wealth buys only superfluities.

rubrics_metrics.name: March to your own drummer—value originality of pace
rubrics_metrics.description: If a man does not keep pace with his companions, perhaps it is because he hears a different drummer. Let him step to the music which he hears, however measured or far away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rush to conform or to 'succeed' on others' timetable; being out of step can indicate unique insight or calling. Anti-pattern: desperate haste to succeed and mimic others' trajectories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a Columbus to the continents within you
rubrics_metrics.description: Be a Columbus to whole new continents and worlds within you, opening new channels, not of trade, but of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize internal exploration and intellectual discovery over external travel or conquest. Practical counsel: explore your own higher latitudes and map your inner world before seeking external fame or exoticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve mystery—not everything must be surveyed
rubrics_metrics.description: At the same time that we are earnest to explore and learn all things, we require that all things be mysterious and unexplorable, that land and sea be infinitely wild, unsurveyed and unfathomed by us because unfathomable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow room for the unresolvable and the mysterious; curiosity should coexist with humility about limits. Anti-pattern: exhausting a subject's mystery by over-analysis or mapping away wonder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to fine observation and sensory detail
rubrics_metrics.description: You may tell by looking at any twig of the forest, ay, at your very wood-pile, whether its winter is past or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use close, concrete observation (twigs, bird calls, pollen, light) to indicate season, mood, and truth in writing; such specifics anchor larger truths and make prose vivid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persist with singleness of purpose in pursuit of perfection
rubrics_metrics.description: His singleness of purpose and resolution, and his elevated piety, endowed him, without his knowledge, with perennial youth... By the time he had smoothed and polished the staff ... he had made a new system in making a staff, a world with full and fair proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dedication, patience, and refusal to compromise can produce work of transcendent quality—though the pursuit may take time, it yields unexpectedly grand results. Anti-pattern: abandoning projects for impatience or compromise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject conformity and the worn ruts of tradition
rubrics_metrics.description: How worn and dusty, then, must be the highways of the world, how deep the ruts of tradition and conformity!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of mental and social grooves that limit thought and action. Strive to form original paths rather than follow beat tracks; the earth and mind are 'soft and impressible' and can be shaped by individual feet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand novelty and resist tolerating dulness
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an incessant influx of novelty into the world, and yet we tolerate incredible dulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate and welcome novelty in thought and expression; do not accept dull, conventional sermons or trite content. Creators should aim to produce work that reflects the ongoing influx of newness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be awake—presence is prerequisite to new days
rubrics_metrics.description: Only that day dawns to which we are awake. There is more day to dawn. The sun is but a morning star.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conscious awareness and wakefulness are necessary to perceive and participate in new opportunities and transformations. Anti-pattern: passivity that lets potential days remain unrealized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer living authenticity over ancestral comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Some are dinning in our ears that we Americans, and moderns generally, are intellectual dwarfs compared with the ancients ... A living dog is better than a dead lion. Shall a man go and hang himself because he belongs to the race of pygmies?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not despair because of historical or cultural limitations; focus on being the best version of yourself now rather than comparing unfavorably to past greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth alone wears well
rubrics_metrics.description: No face which we can give to a matter will stead us so well at last as the truth. This alone wears well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term value in writing and life accrues to truthfulness rather than fashionable styles or transient affectations; invest in truth as durable material for work.
